title: How to start a cafe in Dubai: A practical guide
summary: Learn how to start a cafe in Dubai, including licences, food safety approvals, business planning, taxes, startup costs, and expense management.
body_markdown:
Your cafe idea probably starts with excellent coffee, a menu you love, and a space you can already picture. Then the rent quotation arrives, the equipment supplier sends an estimate, and the paperwork starts piling up.


If you're researching how to start a cafe business in Dubai, you need a plan that covers more than the customer experience. Licensing, food safety, staffing, and cash flow all affect whether your cafe can stay open long enough to build a loyal following.


This guide explains the main setup steps, what to budget for, and what aspiring cafe owners can learn from businesses already operating in the UAE.


## Why Dubai attracts cafe entrepreneurs


Dubai's mix of residents, tourists, and office workers creates opportunities for specialty coffee shops, neighbourhood cafes, dessert bars, and delivery-led food businesses.


Your concept should shape your menu, pricing, location, and staffing. Otherwise, you could end up paying premium rent for a cafe that hasn't decided who its customers are.


## Legal requirements to open a cafe in Dubai


Before signing a lease, check the approvals required for your proposed business activity and premises.


### Get the right business licence


Choose a suitable legal structure and confirm whether a mainland or eligible free zone setup fits your plans. For a physical cafe serving customers in Dubai, start with the[Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism's licensing guidance](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/licences-and-permits) .


### Meet food safety requirements


Dubai Municipality provides the[Food Code and food establishment requirements](https://www.dm.gov.ae/municipality-business/food-traders-establishments/) . Your kitchen layout, storage facilities, food preparation areas, and operating procedures must meet the applicable rules.


Check the required[food establishment design and approval services](https://www.dm.gov.ae/dubai-municipality-services/) before starting construction. Discovering that your kitchen layout needs changes after the fit-out is complete is an expensive way to learn about compliance.


### Plan for staff and taxes


If you hire baristas, chefs, or servers, account for applicable employment permits, visas, training, and other staffing costs.


You should also understand your tax obligations. The[Federal Tax Authority's VAT guidance](https://tax.gov.ae/en/taxes/Vat/vat.topics/registration.for.vat.aspx) states that UAE-resident businesses generally must register when taxable supplies and imports exceed AED 375,000 over the previous 12 months or are expected to exceed that threshold in the next 30 days. Voluntary registration may be available from AED 187,500, subject to the relevant conditions.


## How to start a cafe business in Dubai in six steps


### 1. Research your market


Visit competing cafes at breakfast, lunchtime, and in the evening. Compare prices, menus, customer traffic, and service times.


### 2. Write your cafe business plan


A starting cafe business plan should cover your target customers, menu, pricing, expected sales, suppliers, staffing, and marketing. It should also include startup costs, monthly expenses, cash flow forecasts, and a contingency reserve.


Calculate your break-even point before committing to a lease. For example, if monthly fixed costs are AED 45,000 and your contribution margin is 60%, you need AED 75,000 in monthly sales to cover those fixed costs, before any additional expenses excluded from the calculation.


### 3. Choose your location carefully


Compare rent, footfall, parking, nearby offices and homes, delivery demand, and competition. Confirm that the premises can accommodate your intended food activity before signing.


A busy street can look promising, but passing traffic doesn't guarantee paying customers. Your forecast should account for how many people are likely to buy something, not simply walk past your window.


### 4. Plan your equipment and fit-out


List the equipment your menu actually requires. A coffee-focused cafe may need espresso machines, grinders, refrigeration, and water filtration. A full kitchen will require additional equipment and preparation space.


### 5. Hire staff and test the menu


Train staff on recipes, food safety, customer service, and stock handling. Run practice service before opening to test preparation times, portion sizes, and ingredient costs.


### 6. Launch and track performance


Use local partnerships, social media, and introductory offers to attract customers. Once sales begin, monitor average order value, product margins, ingredient waste, labour costs, and repeat visits.


If one item sells particularly well, check how much it contributes to profit before making it the centrepiece of your marketing. Popularity is useful, but it doesn't pay the supplier by itself.


## What can you learn from UAE cafe businesses?


Hampstead Bakery and Cafe offers an example of testing demand and developing a recognisable concept. A[Gulf News feature published in April 2026](https://gulfnews.com/lifestyle/how-one-uae-cloud-kitchen-became-a-homegrown-success-story-the-power-of-community-and-french-toast-1.500507583) traced its growth from a cloud kitchen into a cafe business.


The report highlights the role of community and distinctive menu items. Its tableside tiramisu, finished with hot chocolate, was identified as a dish that stood out and gained attention online.


## Keep your cafe finances under control


Your cafe will make frequent payments for ingredients, packaging, equipment repairs, utilities, and other operating costs. Without organised records, it's difficult to spot rising costs or understand where your margins are going.


Use a dedicated business account, retain receipts and invoices, and review spending against your budget. Set clear limits for staff purchases and establish approval rules for larger payments.


An[AI-native business bank account from Alaan](https://www.alaan.com/business-banking) can support business payments and expense management.[Alaan SuperCard](https://www.alaan.com/supercard) offers controlled business spending, while[Alaan SuperPay](https://www.alaan.com/superpay) supports international supplier and contractor payments, subject to product terms and eligibility.


These tools can help organise spending, but your underlying numbers still matter. Review cash flow regularly so you know whether you can cover rent, salaries, and supplier invoices without relying on next week's sales.


## Conclusion


Starting a cafe in Dubai takes a clear concept, the right approvals, realistic sales forecasts, and careful expense management. Research your market, confirm your premises can meet food safety requirements, and calculate break-even sales before committing to major costs.


Before opening, ask yourself one question: how many orders do you need each day to cover your costs? If you can answer that with a realistic forecast, you're in a better position to decide whether your cafe idea is ready for investment.


## FAQs


### How much does it cost to open a cafe in Dubai?


Costs depend on location, rent, fit-out, equipment, licensing, staffing, and working capital. Get quotations for your specific concept rather than relying on a generic startup figure.


### Can a foreigner open a cafe in Dubai?


Foreign entrepreneurs can establish businesses in Dubai, subject to applicable ownership, licensing, immigration, and regulatory requirements. Confirm the appropriate structure for your activity.


### Do I need food safety approval?


Yes. You must meet the applicable Dubai Municipality food establishment requirements and obtain the necessary approvals for your premises and activities.


### When should I register for VAT?


UAE-resident businesses generally must register when taxable supplies and imports exceed AED 375,000 over the previous 12 months or are expected to exceed that threshold in the next 30 days. Check the FTA's guidance for the full conditions.


### What should a cafe business plan include?


Include your concept, target customers, menu pricing, startup costs, monthly expenses, expected sales, break-even point, and cash flow forecast. Update your assumptions as actual sales data becomes available.
